leftEvidence.title: Stephen places Solomon’s house under prophetic critique

points.label: Solomon-relative action
points.left: Stephen recalls the wilderness tent, David’s desire, Solomon’s building, and Isaiah’s claim that the Most High does not dwell in handmade houses.
points.right: Solomon praises covenant faithfulness, asks the promise to David to continue, and asks God to hear prayers directed toward the house.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Temple history is honored and relativized within a speech accusing resistant hearers.
points.right: The king stands before the altar and addresses God before the assembly.

payload.posture: Solomon says heaven cannot contain God while asking that prayers toward the house be heard; Stephen cites the same limit in a prophetic accusation.

rightEvidence.title: Solomon asks the uncontainable God to hear

payload.tension: The builder’s own prayer provides a boundary later used to challenge confidence in the building.
payload.title: Solomon’s prayer and Stephen’s Temple critique
